scenes.title: Running & Building dbt
scenes.narration: This lesson covers the everyday dbt commands you use to build models, run tests, and select exactly what to execute.

scenes.title: dbt run versus dbt build

right.heading: dbt build
points: Tests each model right after it builds

scenes.narration: The command dbt run builds your models and nothing else, which makes it convenient for quick iteration while writing SQL. The command dbt build does far more, running models, tests, seeds, and snapshots together in dependency order. Crucially, dbt build tests each model immediately after it is created, so a failure halts downstream work before bad data spreads, which is why it is the preferred command in production.

scenes.title: Selecting what to run
scenes.code:
# Build one model and everything after it
dbt build --select stg_orders+

# Build a model and everything before it
dbt build --select +fct_orders

# Build a whole folder
dbt build --select staging.*
scenes.narration: You rarely need to build the entire project, so dbt gives you graph selectors. A trailing plus sign means build this model and all of its descendants, which is useful after changing something upstream. A leading plus sign means build this model and all of its ancestors, ensuring its inputs are fresh. You can also target an entire folder with a wildcard. Mastering selection is the single biggest way to speed up your development loop.

scenes.title: Other essential commands
bullets: dbt test runs data tests on existing tables
dbt compile renders Jinja into raw SQL
dbt docs generate produces the lineage site
scenes.narration: A few other commands round out daily work. dbt test executes your data quality checks against tables that already exist, dbt compile renders all your Jinja templating into the raw SQL that will actually run so you can inspect it, and dbt docs generate produces the searchable documentation and lineage website.

scenes.title: A typical development loop
scenes.narration: A healthy development loop is tight and focused. You edit one model, build just that model and its descendants so you only pay for what changed, read the results and any failing tests, and repeat until everything is green before committing. Keeping the loop small is what makes dbt development feel fast.

scenes.text: Use dbt build in CI and production so models and their tests always run together in the correct order.
scenes.narration: For continuous integration and production runs, standardize on dbt build so that models and their tests always execute together in the correct dependency order, catching problems before they reach your stakeholders.
